project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
New knowledge, technology, skills or research facilities for low-carbon hydrogen that stay in and strengthen the province of Groningen.
The call aims to increase, spread and retain knowledge about hydrogen in the region, to promote cooperation between knowledge institutions and companies, and to strengthen knowledge institutions structurally. Low-carbon hydrogen covers green hydrogen from renewable electricity and blue hydrogen from natural gas with carbon capture.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 2 · Artikel 2 Doel; Artikel 5 Subsidiabele activiteiten

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Five activities qualify; each has its own minimum score and state-aid basis.
- Experimental or industrial research projects, including modelling, on low-carbon hydrogen (production, transport, storage and use)
- Experimental or industrial development of innovative technologies and processes for the hydrogen chain
- Setting up hydrogen training and education programmes
- Developing internships at companies in the hydrogen industry
- Investments in hydrogen research facilities, such as laboratories, electrolysers or storage test set-ups
Excluded: projects that do not fit the province's Economic Vision and Climate Agenda 2030, projects without benefits mainly in Groningen, projects already started, and costs such as general overheads, marketing, travel and consultancy without direct project relevance.
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 2 · Artikel 5 Subsidiabele activiteiten; Artikel 6 Weigeringsgronden; Artikel 7 Subsidievereisten
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 10 Niet subsidiabele kosten
SNN, Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG) · Veelgestelde vragen (Waar kan ik subsidie ... voor krijgen?)

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
The province's need for a hydrogen ecosystem with enough low-carbon hydrogen to make Groningen's industry sustainable, which requires new knowledge, innovation and skilled people.
The need is regional and public: the provincial Climate Agenda 2030 and Economic Vision, under the Nationaal Programma Groningen (NPG, a national programme that funds the region's future after gas extraction). The project must contribute concretely to the province's policy goals on hydrogen knowledge and innovation; this is a knock-out criterion.
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 1 · Overwegende dat
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 3 · Artikel 8, lid 2b (relevantie voor beleidsdoelen)

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
The research, technology, training, internships or facility, plus a knowledge-sharing and impact-evaluation plan, a business case and public sharing of results.
- A plan for knowledge sharing and for evaluating the project's impact on the hydrogen sector
- A business case with investment and operating budgets per calendar year
- Results and lessons made publicly available and actively shared, including with the province
- Annual progress reports if the project runs longer than 12 months, and a settlement request within 13 weeks of completion
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 4-5 · Artikel 11 Indieningsvereisten; Artikel 17 Verplichtingen van de subsidieontvanger

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Economic and technological development of Groningen's hydrogen sector, CO2 reduction, and a robust hydrogen infrastructure in the long term.
- Regional development: the project must show how it strengthens the regional hydrogen sector and sustainable growth (knock-out).
- Environment: a concrete description of environmental effects such as CO2 reduction (10 points).
- Long term: a contribution to a robust and sustainable hydrogen infrastructure, including scaling up innovations.
- Skills: the number of internships or education programmes and their contribution to the skills the sector needs.
The call sets no numerical targets.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 3-4 · Artikel 8, lid 2b, 2e, 2g and 2h

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
Results must be kept in place for five years after the final settlement, shared publicly, and show potential to scale or be replicated elsewhere.
- Durability: the beneficiary must maintain the results for five years after the decision that settles the subsidy.
- Replication: the project must show concrete potential for larger scale or other regions (10 points); replication during the project is not required.
- Knowledge sharing: results and lessons must be made public and shared actively, including with the province of Groningen.
- Continuity: the project must explain how it builds on earlier initiatives, such as the JTF campus scheme, or how it can serve as a basis for future projects.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 4-5 · Artikel 8, lid 2h and 2i; Artikel 17, onderdelen e, f, i and j

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
A single applicant may apply; a collaboration must have at least two parties.
The call scores cooperation between knowledge institutions and companies (25 points), so a single-applicant project would score lower.
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 2 · Artikel 1, onderdeel j; Artikel 3 Doelgroep
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 3 · Artikel 8, lid 2e

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
Knowledge institutions and companies are expected; governments may also take part.
The criteria assess which knowledge institutions and companies are involved and how they cooperate, and how the project strengthens the knowledge institutions' facilities, research capacity and education (25 points). A company counts only if it has legal personality and contributes to hydrogen knowledge and innovation. The regulation sets no location rule for partners, but the benefits must land mainly in Groningen province.
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 2 · Artikel 1, onderdeel f; Artikel 7
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 3-4 · Artikel 8, lid 2e, 2f and 2i

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The call sets no split of work or budget, but each partner's role and contribution must be clearly described and justified.
A collaboration agreement must describe the roles, responsibilities and financial contributions of all partners. The lead partner (penvoerder) coordinates, administers and acts as contact point.
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 2 · Artikel 1, onderdeel g
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 4 · Artikel 8, lid 2i; Artikel 11, lid 3d

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: A company, knowledge institution or public-law body, or the lead partner of a collaboration, with the consent of all participants.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 2 · Artikel 3 Doelgroep

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Yes, in principle: TenneT may apply or lead a collaboration if it counts as a company contributing to hydrogen knowledge and innovation and the benefits land mainly in Groningen.
The regulation defines a company as one that "bijdraagt aan de kennis- en innovatietrajecten in de waterstofsector" (contributes to knowledge and innovation in the hydrogen sector). TenneT would have to show that link, for example through research on electrolysers' role on the electricity grid. A project led by a knowledge institution or hydrogen company would fit the call's aims better.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 2 · Artikel 1, onderdeel f; Artikel 3 Doelgroep; Artikel 7

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes. TenneT could join a collaboration and carry its own costs, since the applicant must co-finance at least half the project anyway.
The regulation does not describe an unfunded partner role, but every partner's role must be clearly justified.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 3-4 · Artikel 8, lid 2c and 2i

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes, up to 50% of eligible costs, capped by the EU state-aid ceiling for each activity and at EUR 2.5 million per application.
The subsidy is calculated under the General Block Exemption Regulation (AGVV, the EU rules on aid governments may give without notifying Brussels):
- Research and development: articles 25 or 49
- Training and internships: article 31
- Research facilities: article 26
The 50% applies only as far as these state-aid ceilings allow, and it is also the cap when state-aid rules would allow more. Staff costs count only if set with an integral cost system or the government rates handbook. TenneT must finance the rest of its costs itself.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 4-5 · Artikel 9 Subsidiabele kosten; Artikel 14 Subsidiehoogte; Artikel 16 Staatssteun

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
My judgement: TenneT would be useful as the electricity-system partner in a research or modelling project on how large electrolysers in Groningen, for example at Eemshaven, can operate flexibly against grid congestion and renewable supply.
It could provide grid data, connection and congestion scenarios, and system-integration expertise, while a knowledge institution leads the research and a hydrogen producer brings the electrolyser case. This fits the research-and-modelling activity and the call's emphasis on knowledge institutions and cooperation, but it is at the edge of the call's hydrogen-sector focus.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 2 · Artikel 2 Doel; Artikel 5, lid 1

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer:
Research and development projects must be new: the solutions must be a clear advance on the current state of the hydrogen sector and generate new knowledge, methods or skills.
Innovativeness is worth 25 points; it does not apply to training and internship activities.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 3 · Artikel 8, lid 2d

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Technology and processes in the hydrogen chain, and new knowledge, methods and skills, including education programmes.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 2-3 · Artikel 5; Artikel 8, lid 2d

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Industrial research and experimental development (as defined in the EU state-aid rules), plus training, internships and research facilities; demonstration and deployment are not funded as such.
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 2 · Artikel 5 Subsidiabele activiteiten

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: The project must explain how it builds on earlier initiatives, such as projects from the JTF campus scheme, or how it can be a basis for future projects (5 points).
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 8, lid 2i

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer:
The call asks for a concrete description of environmental effects, such as CO2 reduction, and an evaluation of the project's impact on the hydrogen sector.
The evaluation plan must state its specific objectives and how impact will be measured.
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 8, lid 2g; Artikel 11, lid 3c

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
Up to EUR 2.5 million per application, from a EUR 9.9 million budget.
- Total project size: not stated; at the 50% maximum rate the EUR 2.5 million cap corresponds to EUR 5 million of eligible costs (my calculation)
- Grant request: at most EUR 2,500,000 per application; no minimum
- Funding form: a share of eligible costs (external costs and staff costs)
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 5 · Artikel 13 Subsidieplafond; Artikel 14 Subsidiehoogte

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
At most 50% of eligible costs for every activity, and lower where the state-aid article requires.
- Co-financing conditions: the applicant must co-finance at least 50% of the total project costs, in cash or in kind; this is a knock-out criterion
- Evidence required: the co-financing must be clearly shown in the budget; the business case lists own funds, other subsidies and other financing
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 3 · Artikel 8, lid 2c
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 5 · Artikel 14

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Eligible costs depend on the activity's state-aid article; staff costs must follow set cost systems.
- Eligible costs: research and development as in AGVV articles 25 and 49 (staff, equipment, buildings and land, contract research and patents, materials, external experts); training and internships as in article 31; research facilities as in article 26
- Excluded costs: general overheads, marketing and promotion, consultancy without direct project relevance, travel, fines and legal costs, unrelated operating costs and unrelated training
- Overheads and VAT: no general overheads; staff costs only via an integral cost system or the government rates handbook
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 9 Subsidiabele kosten; Artikel 10 Niet subsidiabele kosten
SNN, Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG) · Veelgestelde vragen (Welke kosten zijn subsidiabel?)

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
A 20% advance on request, then advances on costs paid, up to 80% in total.
- Payment model: 20% advance before the work; further advances on costs incurred and paid times the subsidy rate; no advance if financing is not secured
- Financial reporting or audit: settlement request within 13 weeks of completion
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 5-6 · Artikel 18 Bevoorschotting en betaling; Artikel 19 Subsidievaststelling

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: an electronic application through SNN's eLoket Zakelijk, from 20 May 2025 to 1 July 2028; budget goes first come, first served.
- Stage 1 — Full application: through the eLoket with eHerkenning (the Dutch business login) or an eLoket account, in nine steps starting with a quick eligibility scan
- Additional procedure: if the budget threatens to run out on one day, complete applications received that day are ranked by lot
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 4-5 · Artikel 11, lid 1; Artikel 12 Indieningstermijn; Artikel 15 Verdeelcriteria
SNN, Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG) · Aanvraag voorbereiden (Stappenplan)

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
Start within one year of the grant and carry out the activities before 1 July 2029.
- Maximum duration: four years, according to the SNN page
- Required start: within one year of the grant decision, and not before the application
- Completion deadline: activities completed before 1 July 2029
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 5 · Artikel 17, onderdelen a, c and d
SNN, Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG) · Wat zijn de voorwaarden?

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The provincial rules set a decision within 13 weeks of receipt, or 22 weeks if advice is sought or further investigation is needed.
- Conditions before starting: a collaboration agreement for collaborations
cards.sources:
Procedureregeling subsidies provincie Groningen 2018.pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 2.4 Beslistermijnen subsidieverlening
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 11, lid 3d

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
A project plan and budget in SNN's format for the chosen activity, plus annexes.
- Application form: project plan in the format for the activity (research and modelling, development, training, internships, or facilities), with a description at activity level
- Budget: SNN budget format for the activity
- Mandatory annexes: knowledge-sharing and impact-evaluation plan; business case with investment and operating budgets per year; state-aid analysis for the relevant AGVV article; collaboration agreement where relevant
- Partner documents: proof of signing authority, SME declaration, statement on financial difficulties signed by hand, previous year's (consolidated) annual accounts, partner details form signed by hand
- Registration: eHerkenning or an eLoket account
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 11 Indieningsvereisten
SNN, Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG) · Aanvraag voorbereiden (Dit heb je nodig voor je aanvraag)

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Applications must pass three knock-out criteria and reach a minimum score that depends on the activity.
- Knock-out criteria: feasibility (technical, organisational, financial stability, risk management); relevance to provincial policy goals; at least 50% co-financing
- Evaluation criteria and weighting: innovativeness 25; cooperation and knowledge sharing 25; strengthening knowledge institutions 25; sustainability and long-term impact 10; added value for the hydrogen sector 10; integration and coherence 5
- Thresholds: 70 points for research, development and facilities; 40 for training; 23 for internships
- Ranking rules: first come, first served from the day the application is complete; ties on the day the budget runs out are decided by lot
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 3-5 · Artikel 8 Beoordelingscriteria; Artikel 15 Verdeelcriteria

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Some criteria apply only to particular activities.
- Exception — training and internships: innovativeness, sustainability and sector added value do not apply; internships are also exempt from the policy-relevance and knowledge-institution criteria
- Conditional — financing not secured: no advance is paid
- Recommended: link the project to earlier initiatives such as the JTF campus scheme
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Waterstof kennisontwikkeling en innovatie (NPG).pdf · pp. 3-5 · Artikel 8; Artikel 18, lid 2
